# Sevilla Veterinary Hospital

> Veterinary hospital for dogs and cats at 2116 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA 90405, founded by Dr. Antonio Pedraza, DVM, MVM, cert SAS, MRCVS. Wellness exams, vaccinations, dentistry, senior care, urgent care during business hours, physical therapy and advanced surgery: TPLO and orthopedics, laparoscopy, soft tissue and brachycephalic (BOAS) airway surgery.

## Key facts
- Name: Sevilla Veterinary Hospital (also "Sevilla Vet"; sometimes written "Seville Veterinary Hospital")
- Address: 2116 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA 90405, United States (on Main Street, a craftsman house a few blocks from the beach)
- Phone: (310) 310-3704 · Email: info@sevillavet.com
- Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 6:00 pm. Closed Saturday and Sunday; the phone is still answered. Surgical drop-off 8:00 to 9:30 am.
- Patients: dogs and cats
- Exams: $60 pet exams for new and existing clients
- Referrals: free consultations for potential surgical referrals
- Online appointments: https://petportal.vet/sevilla-veterinary-hospital
- Parking: metered street parking in front of the hospital (most spaces up to 3 hours); ramp access at the entrance
- Not a 24-hour hospital. After-hours emergencies: Veterinary Emergency Group – Santa Monica, 2700 Wilshire Boulevard, Santa Monica, CA 90403, (424) 538-4535, open 24/7
- Payment: financing options; works with all pet insurance carriers
- Online pharmacy: Mixlab (exclusive partner), delivery in 1 to 2 days in Los Angeles
- Areas served: Santa Monica, Venice, Ocean Park, Marina del Rey and the wider Los Angeles area
- Profiles: Instagram https://www.instagram.com/sevillavet/ · Facebook https://www.facebook.com/p/Sevilla-Veterinary-Hospital-61564454010015/ · Yelp https://www.yelp.com/biz/sevilla-veterinary-hospital-santa-monica
- In the press: VoyageLA interview with Dr. Pedraza, 3 February 2026: https://voyagela.com/interview/exploring-life-business-with-antonio-pedraza-of-sevilla-veterinary-hospital/
- Content last updated: 27 October 2026. Pages show an "Updated" date and cite independent veterinary sources (ACVS, AAHA, WSAVA, AVMA, ASPCA, FDA, University of Cambridge BOAS Research Group, Royal Veterinary College).

## Veterinarians
- Dr. Antonio Pedraza Reales, DVM, MVM, cert SAS, MRCVS: founder; born in Sevilla (Seville), Spain; postgraduate surgical training in the United Kingdom (ESPVS, BSAVA) focused on orthopedics, spinal and complex soft tissue surgery; extensive endoscopy and laparoscopy training; Master's in Small Animal Surgery & Traumatology (Madrid); former instructor of laparoscopic procedures in Europe; more than 20 years of surgical experience
- Dr. Gabriella Robbins, DVM: Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine (2018), clinical training at Oregon State University; diagnostics, preventive care, internal medicine and soft tissue surgery
- Dr. Holly Jordan, DVM: Western University of Health Sciences; internal medicine and preventive care

## Surgery facts
- TPLO for cranial cruciate ligament rupture; TTA and CBLO for selected cases; lateral suture no longer performed. Most dogs go home the same day or the next day. Recovery 2 to 3 months, x-rays at 6 to 8 weeks. One all-inclusive quote including post-operative x-rays and rechecks.
- Orthopedic pain control: epidural for hind-limb procedures (24 hours) plus Nocita local anesthetic (up to 72 hours); titanium implants and bone graft with every orthopedic procedure.
- Laparoscopic spay: one or two dime-sized incisions, up to 65% less post-operative pain, recovery usually 5 to 7 days (14 to 21 after a traditional spay), intradermal sutures with nothing to remove. Usually done after the first heat cycle (2 to 3 weeks after it ends).
- Laparoscopic gastropexy prevents bloat (GDV) in at-risk large, deep-chested breeds and can be combined with a spay or cryptorchid neuter. Laparoscopic cryptorchid neuter and laparoscopic (mostly liver) biopsy are also offered.
- BOAS surgery for bulldogs, French bulldogs, pugs and other flat-faced breeds: widening the nostrils and shortening the soft palate; ventilators and advanced anesthesia protocols.
- Same-day surgery: morning fasted consultations and surgery the same day when medically appropriate; overnight monitoring on select days.
- Soft tissue surgery: head and neck (cherry eye, TECA, rhinoplasty), abdomen (pyometra, splenectomy, cystotomy, gastrotomy and enterotomy, hernias, mass removal) and chest (lung lobectomy, pericardectomy); Nocita for every procedure.
- Wellness: puppy and kitten series, adult and senior exams, dental cleaning under anesthesia with pre-anesthetic bloodwork; vaccination schedules follow WSAVA and AAHA guidance.
- Urgent care is during business hours only; the hospital is not a 24-hour emergency facility.
